chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'And when they fall on their sides' [22:36]. He said: If they fall (lifeless) on the ground, then eat from it. 'And feed the needy and the beggar' [22:36]. He said: The needy (al-Qa'in) is the one who is pleased with what you give him, does not become angry, does not frown, nor makes scum fill his mouth corner out of anger. And the beggar (al-Mu'tarr) is the one who passes by you whom you feed.

key_terms.الْقَانِع: The needy; one who is content and dignified in receiving
key_terms.الْمُعْتَر: The beggar; one who passes by and is fed
key_terms.يَزْبِدُ شَدَقَهُ: To make scum/foam fill the corner of the mouth (from anger or excitement)
key_terms.يَكْلَح: To frown or show displeasure in the face

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the needy and the beggar in Quranic exegesis according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the distinction between the *Qa'in* and the *Mu'tarr* within the context of animal sacrifice, emphasizing the etiquette of receiving charity. The *Qa'in* is characterized by dignified contentment and the absence of visible displeasure, whereas the *Mu'tarr* is defined by the casual act of passing by to receive sustenance. This interpretation highlights the Shia emphasis on preserving the recipient's dignity and the specific social dynamics of almsgiving in early Islamic society.
